title: Writ against post-checking assessment dismissed for s.127 appeal
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Sunil Ambwani and Pankaj Naqvi, JJ.
disposition: Writ dismissed; relegated to s.127 appeal against assessment.
headnote: After a checking that found unauthorised use, an FIR under Section 135, and a Supply Code assessment and demand, the High Court dismissed the writ because Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 supplies an appeal against the assessment and demand order.
facts: Checking on 5 May 2011 found the petitioner unauthorisedly drawing electricity to run a 3 HP motor for a flour mill. An FIR under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 was lodged and a provisional assessment of Rs. 60,831 was proposed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. He objected that the mill ran on a 10 HP generator and the 3 HP residential motor was used sparingly. The Executive Engineer re-inspected, confirmed the earlier report, and rejected the objections on 28 January 2012. He then filed this writ.

holding_units.topic: writ against assessment barred by s.127 appeal
holding_units.holding: Where an assessment and demand follow a checking that found unauthorised use and an FIR under Section 135, the consumer’s remedy against that assessment and demand is an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; a writ petition is dismissed on the ground of that alternative remedy.

not_decided.point: Merits of the unauthorised-use finding and the quantum of assessment
not_decided.note: Objections that the mill ran on a generator were not decided; the Court noted there were no objections to method or quantum and left the assessment to the s.127 appeal.
